v1.feedback: The differential-growth ribbon rising into a dandelion-clock dispersal is a strong concept that lands the linked idea well, and the inherited risograph posterize shader gives it printmaking warmth. Two things to refine: the 3-tone posterization may flatten the seed pappus cloud into near-invisibility against the light band — consider adding a fourth mid-light tone or slightly widening the luminance thresholds so seeds read as distinct from the ribbon surface. Second, 280 seeds at size 2.5–6 may feel sparse for a full clock blow; bumping to ~400 seeds with a tighter initial burst cone before they drift would sell the 'exhale' moment more dramatically.

v2.feedback: The differential-growth ribbon rising into a seed-exhale is a legible dandelion-clock concept, and the 4-band risograph posterize is a smart nod to the color_quantization parent branch. The earth-tone palette (gold ribbon, indigo-to-cream bands) and gentle disperse motion are well-tuned. Two refinements: the FogExp2 density at 0.018 may swallow the upper crown and drifting seeds before they read—drop it to ~0.008 or fade fog only beyond the seed travel radius; and the ribbon at 1400 max verts may stay too thin/abstract to read as a dandelion head in the first 2 seconds—consider splitting the growth ring into 3–4 stacked rings at slightly different heights so the crown reads as a spherical puff before the exhale begins.
